blocks.text: Every value has a **type**, and the type decides how much memory the value takes and which values it can hold. Whole-number types: `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64` (signed, `i` = integer) and `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64` (unsigned, so never negative). The number is the bit width. For fractions there are `f32` and `f64`.
If you write no type, whole numbers are `i32` and fractions are `f64`. To state the type yourself, write `name: type = value`.
Use `_` to make big numbers readable. `0x` starts a hexadecimal number and `0b` a binary one.
`usize` is the type used for array lengths and indexes; you will see it often later.

blocks.prompt: Make an `f64` variable named `radius` equal to 2.0. Print `radius * radius * 3.0`.

blocks.q: Which type is an 8-bit whole number that can never be negative?
